title: Naturality of the first Tor identification with the ideal-tensor kernel
statement: Let $f:R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $J=IA\subseteq A$, $M$ an $R$-module, $N$ an $A$-module, and $g:M\to N$ an additive map satisfying $g(rx)=f(r)g(x)$ for all $r\in R$, $x\in M$. Write $\mu_R:I\otimes_RM\to M$, $a\otimes x\mapsto ax$, and $\mu_A:J\otimes_AN\to N$, $b\otimes y\mapsto by$. The short exact sequences $0\to I\to R\to R/I\to0$ and $0\to J\to A\to A/J\to0$ give natural isomorphisms $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,R/I)\simeq\ker\mu_R$ and $\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(N,A/J)\simeq\ker\mu_A$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Under these isomorphisms, the change-of-rings map on Tor induced by $f$ and $g$ agrees with the restriction of $I\otimes_RM\to J\otimes_AN$, $a\otimes x\mapsto f(a)\otimes g(x)$, to the kernels.
